The meaning of the word is tied to human biology. And our biology is the objective truth that most consistently applies to the most of us. Meaning that at the base of our physical existence, the overwhelming majority of us have XX or XY chromosomes. We’re either male or female. Intersex is where that consistency breaks down, but that’s still biological, which will always be exponentially more consistent than categories based on gender identity. 

To the other side of this issue, ‘woman’ refers to anyone that simply identifies as a woman. This is a supplemental definition of the word, in which biology has nothing to do with being a woman. It’s merely a state of mind, where the individual essentially defines the term. And the individual defining the term, of course, undermines the fundamental purpose of language. Words have a defined meaning, so we can all communicate with precision & specificity.

The words ‘male’ & ‘female’ are important words, b/c they’re foundational to our being. Males & females have specific roles that are essential to the proliferation & survival of our species. That’s why the biological relationship between male & female has been the framework of human civilization— for all time. Males & females are different. They’re our most basic categories, and until the 90s, ‘male’ has always been exclusively synonymous to ‘man’, and ‘female’ to ‘woman’, with respect to human being. Most of us still make those direct associations— exclusively. And that’s what makes gender ideology incongruent with most of society. 

At the core, biological sex is natural order. Whereas gender, as I’ve come to understand it, is culturally derived, and includes an ever-expanding variety of identities across a spectrum that includes masculinity, femininity, both, and neither, all of which may or may not correspond with biological sex, and may or may not be fluid within and/or outside of any given individual expression. 

So basically, according to gender identity, a male is not always a man, and a female is not always a woman. We can see the problems that this is going to create with people that have believed, as relatively everyone prior to the 1990s believed, that a male is a man, and a female is a woman. 

The proponents of this ideology are asking us to replace biology with psychology, in terms of how we organize ourselves in society. They want society to prioritize what one feels like being, over one’s actual being. The fundamental problem with this is that the human imagination is fluid & boundless, and doesn’t always comport with the objective truth in the physical reality we all have to share.

A society relies on order. Order in a free society relies on a common truth. Our biology is our common truth. That’s why it’s been the framework of human civilization— for all time. It affords us the fixed categories that most consistently correspond with the objective truth in this physical reality we all have to share. It gives us the categories that most consistently apply to the most of us— the most rational & practical categories by which to organize ourselves in society. 

If society embraced this gender ideology, we’d be replacing order with chaos. Our common truth would be that we have no common truth; that there could be as many possible categories as there are people. It would be a disaster, and would eventually require an arduous course correction, assuming it didn’t topple the existing system first. It’s one of the worst ideas in human history.
